text: A password is a secret that keeps your phone, email and photos private. People change it when they think someone has seen it, or just every few months. A good password has a minimum of twelve letters, numbers or signs, and it is not your birthday or your dog's name. Some people write a password on a slice of paper, but a password manager is safer. At lunch with friends, don't type a password where others can see. People ask their phone for changes with words like "lock my phone after one minute", "make my password longer", or "who can see my photos?"

Margaux was a student, and the wifi at her flat was slow again. Her big brother was streaming a game in the next room, and her paper would not upload. A wheel of cheese sat on her desk, forgotten. She spoke to her phone. "Wifi password." The assistant showed the password for the home network and read it out. Her friend Noor was visiting, so Margaux said, "Email it to Noor." The assistant wrote a short email with the network name and the password and sent it. Then Margaux said, "Pause my brother's laptop for an hour." The assistant paused his connection on the router. The page loaded fast, and Margaux finished her paper before dinner.

name: bedtime_planner
does: Picks a bedtime that fits your wake-up time, reminds you to shower and put your phone away, and shows a weekly sleep chart you can print on paper.
inputs: the time you wake up, the hours of sleep you want, and whether it is still light outside
people say:
- What time should I go to bed if I wake up at six?
- I want eight hours of sleep, when do I start winding down?
- Remind me tonight when it's time to get ready for bed
- I keep going to sleep too late, can you help?
- Tell me how I slept this week

Jomar was a retired teacher, and every evening he liked to read. Tonight his tea was sour because he had forgotten the sugar, but he did not mind. "Remind me to read at eight every night," he told the smart speaker. "But I don't want a loud alarm. My wife is already asleep." The assistant set a reminder for eight with a soft chime. Then Jomar asked, "How many pages a day do I need to finish this book by the end of July?" The assistant worked it out and said about twenty. Jomar liked to carry his e-reader out to the garden, so he asked it to open the book where he had stopped. It did, and he did not have to start again from chapter one.

Gabriela had just moved to the city with her two boys. After a long walk to the new school, her feet were sore, and she had to stand on the bus all the way home. At home she sat down and spoke to her phone. "Cut the boys' screen time in half on school days." The assistant changed the limit from two hours to one hour. Then she said, "Tell me a bedtime story that is a bit shorter than last night's." The assistant chose a story of ten minutes. Tomorrow the class would march in the town parade, so she also asked, "Wake the boys twenty minutes earlier than usual." The assistant moved the alarm, and Gabriela finally felt a little less lost.

Fergus drove a delivery van, and the rainy week had been long. In the evening he sat in the cab with his scarf around his neck and spoke to his phone. "Could you please remind me about my daughter's maths homework at seven tonight? I have a late delivery, and I always forget until she is already asleep." The assistant set a reminder for seven and said it would repeat it ten minutes later if he did not answer. Fergus also asked when the sheet was due. The assistant looked at her school list and said Friday. The forecast said it might snow on Friday, so Fergus asked it to add a note to finish the homework a day early.

Going to the movies starts with a simple question: what is on? An assistant can show you the films near you today, with cinema times and a trailer for each one. People change the day, the cinema or the kind of film by saying things like "show me tomorrow's times", "replace that one with a comedy", or "something safe for the kids". At home, many people watch a trailer first and then say "dim the lamp, we're starting the movie." The point is to find something you want to see, at a time that works, without reading a long list yourself.

Zara was seven, and she noticed that her dad kept coughing. The house felt dusty. She went to the speaker in the living room. "Turn on the air purifier and make it a bit quieter," she said. The assistant started the purifier and lowered the fan speed. Later, Zara was playing in the yard when she saw gray smoke far away to the north. She ran inside and asked, "Close the vents and tell me if the air outside is bad." The assistant closed the vents and said the air was a little smoky today. Her dad smiled and said, "Good thinking, Zara. You helped the whole family."

name: gift_finder
does: Suggests gift ideas for a birthday, from a burger dinner to a blue sweater, and tells you where to buy them.
inputs: who the gift is for, what they like, how much you can spend, and where they live
people say:
- I need a present for my dad
- What should I get my sister for her birthday?
- Any ideas for a gift under twenty dollars?
- My friend turns thirty next week and I have no idea what to buy
- Something nice for a coworker who is leaving

Ximena was ten, and she wanted to chill on the sofa. But her phone kept buzzing. She and her aunt ran a page for the family cat, Mochi, and it had many followers. Every like made a noise, and the page felt too busy. "Stop the like alerts and bring them back in two weeks," Ximena said to her phone. The assistant turned them off and set a note for two weeks later. Then she said, "Post the photo of Mochi tomorrow at noon, and write: down one pound!" The assistant saved the post and scheduled it. Ximena put the phone down and finally had some quiet.

Meal planning means deciding what to eat for the week before you go shopping. It saves time and money, and it ends the "what's for dinner?" stress at six o'clock. People with a busy job often plan on Sunday. They change the plan all the time: "make Tuesday vegetarian", "swap the fish for chicken", "add a packed lunch for Thursday". Fancy dinners are rare, but when friends are invited, people say "plan a dinner for six on Saturday." An assistant can write the plan and the shopping list so you do not have to.

A bill is a request for money for something you used, like electricity, water or the internet. Each one has an amount and a due date. Paying on time keeps the lights on and avoids extra fees. People keep a list of bills and change it often: "move the water bill to the first of the month", "remind me three days before rent is due", "take the phone bill off the list". Some people give each kind a color, and purple might mean rent. The electricity bill goes up with the power every outlet in your home uses, so switching things off helps.

Hodan was late for work, and the flat felt stuffy. She ran past the tall plant by the door, grabbed her bag and called out to the speaker. "Run the air purifier until I'm back, and remind me this Saturday afternoon to change the filter." The assistant started the purifier on high and set the reminder. Her allergies were bad, so she took a dose of her medicine with her coffee on the way out. "Also, cool the bedroom a little," she added from the stairs. The assistant lowered the heat by two degrees, and Hodan ran for the bus.

Layla came home after a rough night shift. The house was cold, and her dog, Biscuit, sat by his empty bowl. She dropped her bag and said, "It's freezing in here." The assistant turned the heat up by three degrees. Layla looked at Biscuit and sighed. "He hasn't had breakfast, and I can barely keep my eyes open." The assistant understood and started the pet feeder with one portion, then turned on the lamp by the couch. When Biscuit was eating, Layla asked it to boost the water fountain to the full setting, because it was almost empty. Then she lay down and slept.

Colin was a gardener, and he had filmed a short video of his roses. The shed was dim, and the phone screen glared. "Dim the screen," he said, and the assistant lowered the brightness. Then he asked it to play the clip again. At the end there was one big flower, red as a star. Colin wanted to show it to his sister. "Send this video to Rosa the day after tomorrow in the morning." The assistant scheduled the message. Colin put the phone in his pocket and went back to his plants, happy that his sister would see the roses.

Ruta was a cook, and her hands were wet from the sink. Her close friend Elena had a birthday on Friday. Ruta grabbed her phone from the shelf next to the washer and typed fast: "remind me to pak elena's cake friday morning". The assistant understood and set a reminder for Friday at nine: pack Elena's cake. Ruta smiled and typed one more line. "any gift ideas for elena, she loves tea". The assistant suggested a tea set, a jar of honey, or a nice mug, and said each one could be ordered today. Ruta chose the tea set and went back to her dishes.

Gustavo owned a small shop, and he worked late. When he left the shop it was already dark, and he was tired. In the car he wanted to hear about the game. "What was the score of the Tigers game? No, sorry, I meant the Lions." The assistant said the Lions had won two to one. Gustavo smiled. "Set an alarm for training at six. No, make it half past six." The assistant set the alarm for six thirty. Before bed, Gustavo asked it to remind him to bring the team shirts to the shop on Monday, and the assistant said it would.

A focus timer helps you work for a short time and then rest. Many people work for twenty-five minutes and take a five-minute break. The break is for your eyes, your back and your head. If your neck is sore, stand up and stretch. Let some air blow in through the window, or sit near a vent. People change the timer often: "make it thirty minutes", "add a longer break", "skip the break today". Others like a routine, so they say "start my morning routine at seven." It is a simple way to get things done without getting tired.

Arjun was running for the train. He wanted to visit his grandmother, but the ticket was expensive, so he had to pick the right day. "Days until Sunday," he panted into his phone. "Three days," said the assistant. The ticket was cheaper on Sunday. Arjun counted on his fingers and nodded. "Her birthday is tomorrow," he said to himself, "so I must buy her a present today." He asked the phone, "Gift shop near me?" The assistant showed a shop two streets away. Arjun jumped on the train, and he planned to buy a scarf there before he left the next day.

Emi, a retired teacher, sat in her cozy chair with a blanket on her knees. She said to the television, "Could you please record the cooking show on the third channel tonight? I will be at choir practice, and I don't want to miss the cake lesson." The assistant said it would record the show at eight and keep it for her. Emi was pleased. Then she asked, "Please track that show, so it records every week." The assistant set up the recording to repeat every Thursday. When Emi came home from choir, the cake lesson was waiting for her.

Wendy ran a flower shop, and she had a call with her supplier at ten. She stood by the shop window and spoke to her phone. "Join my ten o'clock call, and make the volume louder. It was half as loud as yesterday." The assistant joined the call and raised the volume. The supplier's words were still hard to understand, so Wendy said, "Share the order list on the screen, and turn on captions." Now she could read every word. "Sorry I'm late," she told the supplier, and they began to talk about next week's roses.

Many people start the day with coffee or tea. How strong or sweet it is depends on the person. A student might want a strong coffee before an exam, while someone else likes a gentle tea with a little honey. When people ask for changes, they say "make it weaker", "less sugar", "a bit more milk", or "just half a cup". A smart coffee machine can remember your usual drink and make it the same way each morning. Some people pack a flask for the day and ask the machine to fill it before they go.

Tesfaye had a job in the morning and a camping trip right after. The day was sunny, and he was late. He threw his bag in the car and called out to his phone, "Make a packing list for two nights, and add twice as many socks as last time." The assistant made the list. "Flash it on the car screen," said Tesfaye, and the list appeared. Then he asked, "Will it rain less in the hills than here?" The assistant said the hills would be sunny too, with a little cloud in the evening. Tesfaye started the car and drove off.

The person wants to know if a home remedy such as vinegar is safe to use for a small health problem.
Is vinegar safe for a sore throat?
Can I gargle with vinegar?
Vinegar on a bee sting, okay?
Will vinegar hurt my skin?
I have a rash, is it safe to put vinegar water on it?
I plan to visit the clinic before lunch on Sunday, so can I try vinegar on my foot until then?
Is that fine for kids too?
Could you please tell me whether vinegar is safe for someone with a weak stomach?

Person: hey how much is 200 in pounds
Assistant: Which currency are you starting from?
Person: us dollars. im going to london in ten days
Assistant: At today's rate, 200 dollars is about 160 pounds. The rate moves, so it may be a little different in ten days.
Person: ok. is winter a good time to go? i want to climb the hills out west
Assistant: I can only help with prices and rates, so I can't say if it is a good time to go. Sorry about that.
Person: no worries, thanks

A smart speaker is a small speaker that listens for a name, like "hey speaker", and then does what a person asks. It can play music, set timers and answer questions. People change its volume, its voice and the room it plays in. You can say "louder", "a bit quieter" or "play it in the kitchen too". If the speaker cannot hear you, say it again a little closer. When a hungry person asks, "set a timer for ten minutes for the pasta", the speaker counts down and rings when the food is ready.

The person wants a dozen dumplings delivered to the back door and says the driver is welcome to leave them there.
Order a dozen dumplings
Get me a dozen dumplings delivered, please
I'm hungry, can I get dumplings sent over?
Dumplings to the back door, a dozen of them
I need more dumplings than last time, make it a dozen
Send twelve dumplings from the place on Park Street
Could you please order a dozen dumplings and tell the driver to come to the back door, because the front bell is broken?

Ligaya was not good with technology, and her inbox was a mess. She stood in the kitchen next to her dirty apron, which hung on a hook by the door, and spoke to her tablet. "Read email." The assistant read three new messages out loud. The second one was from the power company. "Label it bills," said Ligaya. The assistant added the label bills to that message and told her it was done. Ligaya smiled. For the first time in weeks, she knew where her important mail was, and she did not have to press a single button.

Rizal was not good with technology. He pressed the side button on his phone again and again, but nothing happened. Then he remembered he could just talk. "Move my dentist appointment to Thursday and tell me what else I have that day." The assistant moved the appointment and said he had a lunch with his cousin from the east side at noon. Rizal had tried to change the date on the clinic's website earlier, but he could not find the right page. Now it was done in a few seconds. He laughed and said thank you to the phone.

Wanjiru had just moved to the city, and she did not know the shops yet. She wanted to stretch her money, so she asked her phone for a meal plan. "Plan dinners for the week, but no fish and nothing spicy." The assistant planned five dinners with rice, beans, eggs and vegetables. Wanjiru felt silly, because she had never planned a week of food before. Then she said, "I don't want to buy a whole chicken. Only half a chicken, if the shop sells it." The assistant changed the list and found a small market near her flat that sold chicken by the half.

name: pantry_check
does: Checks what is running low in your kitchen, builds a shopping list, and shows the direction to the closest store, with one click to send the list to your phone.
inputs: the food you have at home, how much you use each week, and your address; a square photo of the fridge helps
people say:
- Are we out of milk?
- What do I need from the shop?
- Make me a shopping list for the week
- Is there any butter left?
- I'm at the store, what was I supposed to get?

A recipe tells you how much of each thing to use for a number of servings. Grandma's cake may serve eight, but tonight you may need only four. Scaling a recipe means making every amount bigger or smaller. People measure in cups and spoons, so a cook says "half the recipe", "double it" or "make it for six". An assistant can do the sums and read out the new amounts. Cooks also use timers, like "wake me in thirty minutes" while the dough rests, so nothing is forgotten.

Li came home after a long night shift and sat down at the kitchen table, very tired. "Book a checkup with Dr. Patel and remind me to take my vitamin at nine," she said to her phone. The assistant found a free time on Tuesday and booked it. The clinic's website asked her to scan her insurance card, so she held the card up to the camera, and the assistant sent it. "Pick the day with the least waiting," she added. The assistant said Tuesday morning was the quietest. Li put her head on her arm and smiled.

The person wants to book a haircut that fits their current plan for the day.
Book me a haircut
Haircut today, but not after five
I need a cut, anything except Monday
Can I get an appointment at the barber? Nothing too early, please.
Find a slot for a trim that totals no more than forty minutes, and not on a Saturday
Please book a trim, and I don't want to wait in a long line
I would like a haircut this week, but please don't book it during my lunch break

Many people let a robot mower cut the lawn while they rest. It goes out on a schedule and drives back to its base when it is done. Grass that is damp after rain is hard to cut, so people say "skip mowing today" or "mow after lunch". Other changes are "make the grass shorter", "cut the edges" and "water the front lawn for ten minutes". A sprinkler can also run on a timer. If a mower breaks soon after you buy it, you can ask the shop for a refund.

name: ride_planner
does: Plans a bike route of the distance you like, finds quiet roads, and cancels the plan if it rains.
inputs: where you start, how far you want to go, how many people ride (a mother with a small child needs an easy route), and the day
people say:
- Plan a ride for Saturday morning
- Where can I bike for about twenty kilometers?
- Find me a flat route, I'm not good with hills
- I want an easy loop near the river
- Cancel tomorrow's ride, it's pouring

The person is lucky enough to have an assistant, and wants the day's top headlines read out so they can pay attention to the road with both hands on the wheel.
News
Headlines
What's going on today?
Read me the news
Tell me what happened in the world today
Anything big in the news?
Got any good news? I could use some luck.
I'm driving, could you please read me the top stories from this morning?

The person wants to know how much electricity the home has used this week, now that the meter has had time to sync.
Power use?
Energy today
How much electricity did we use?
Show my usage for the week
What's the bill going to be like this month?
How much power did the house use over the holiday? It was quiet with nobody home
Could you please tell me how much energy we used yesterday compared with the day before?

Francesca had just moved to the city. Her pasta was cooked, and she was packing a lunch for tomorrow when she remembered her bank. "What's my balance?" she asked her phone. The assistant read it out. "Move fifty from savings to checking at half past six," she said, because her rent was due that evening. The assistant scheduled the transfer. The kitchen was sunny, and the screen was hard to read. "Turn up the brightness," said Francesca, and the assistant did. She ate her pasta and felt a little more at home.

name: game_night_helper
does: Keeps score and a turn timer for board games, adds up play money after tax in shop games, and reads the rule when players start a juicy argument.
inputs: the game's name, the players' names, how long each turn lasts, and the time your guests arrive
people say:
- Keep score for Monopoly
- Who is winning?
- Start a two minute timer for Mia's turn
- How do you win at this game?
- Is it okay to trade on the first turn?

The person wants to call their friend Sam on speakerphone while carrying a black bag up the stairs.
Call Sam on speaker
Phone Sam, hands free
Ring Sam
I can't fit the phone and the bag in my hands, call Sam for me
Sam's number ends in fifty, call that one on speaker
Could you please call Sam and put it on speaker, because I'm carrying things up the stairs?

Haruto had just woken up, and his head was foggy. He reached for his phone. "Book a ride to the station for tomorrow at seven." The assistant booked a car with a pickup on the corner of Maple Street. Then Haruto remembered that his new phone did not have the taxi app. "Install the taxi app," he mumbled, and the assistant did. He also had a flight in ten days. "Book a ride to the airport in ten days, early, because I have to board at nine." The assistant saved the booking. Haruto was glad it was all so easy, and he went to make some tea.

Jomar was a student, and he had to read a book for class. A woman at the library had told him the book was funny, so he was looking forward to it. He sat on a bench in the park and said to his phone, "Open chapter three." The assistant opened chapter three of the e-book. After a page he got hungry for a break. "Bookmark here." The assistant saved the page. Then Jomar said, "Set timer," and the assistant started a twenty-minute reading timer. When it rang, he had finished the whole chapter and was laughing.

Agnieszka was nine, and her grandpa had a bad cough. His medicine was on the kitchen table. "Remind Grandpa to take his pill in an hour," Agnieszka said to the speaker. The assistant set the reminder. Then she asked, "How do we get to the doctor's office?" The assistant showed a route by bus and said the ride took about twenty minutes. Grandpa was cold, so she said, "Keep his electric blanket on low." The assistant turned the blanket on at the lowest setting. Grandpa smiled and said she was the best helper in the house.

Person: Resume please.
Assistant: Do you mean the podcast or the audiobook?
Person: Audiobook. I'm cooking crispy chicken.
Assistant: Okay, playing chapter nine from where you stopped.
Person: Can you split this chapter into two parts?
Assistant: Sorry, I can't split a chapter. I can pause it in ten minutes, if you like.
Person: Yes, pause in ten.
Assistant: Done. I will stop it in ten minutes.

Locks keep a home safe. An old lock uses an iron key, but a smart lock uses a code or your phone. A doorbell camera can upload a short clip to your phone when a person comes to the door. People change who may come in by saying things like "lock the front door", "open the garage", "give Sam a code for Friday" or "who is at the door?" It all works well as long as the battery is charged. If the battery is low, the app tells you, so you can change it before you are locked out.

People follow a sports team to know when it plays and how it is doing. A phone can show live scores, the next match and training times. People change what they follow with words like "follow the Hawks", "tell me the score every ten minutes" or "stop the alerts after nine". When a game is going well, fans want the score often. A coach may say the team is going in the right direction when training goes well. Runners and swimmers use the same tools to see their own times and plan the next session.

Nathan had just moved to the city, and his budget was tight. He wanted to order twelve bread rolls for a party and needed to know the price. "Multiply twelve by four," he said to his phone. "No, wait, twelve by five." The assistant said sixty. "Now divide that by three," said Nathan. "Twenty." He was glad the phone had kept up with his change of mind. He wrote the number in his notes, a safe place where he would not lose it, and then went to order the rolls at the shop around the corner.

News is a short report of what happened today. A headline is the title at the head of a story, and it is short enough to read in the blink of an eye. People pick the topics they care about, like sports, weather or local news. They change the list by saying "show me sports news", "only local news", "read the first three" or "any news since this morning?" News about a cold snap or a storm can matter right away, so many people also turn on alerts for those.
